utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Mr. Stevanovic, last week you had access to documents and photographs in order to consider or reconsider the position about certain things. So far as the documents are concerned showing the presence of MUP/Skorpions in the area of Srebrenica and Jahorina at the time of the Srebrenica massacre, what's the position?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to answer the obligation I had taken with respect to checking out some of the data?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... know whether you are now in a position to accept that the documents are what they purport to be.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not in a position to accept that those documents show that the members of the group that we saw on the photograph at that time belonged to the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Let's deal with it in smaller topics. Forget for the time being the video. Just focus, please, on the documents that you were inclined to challenge, documents that showed presence of MUP or Skorpions in the area of Srebrenica, Jahorina. Are you now able to accept that those documents are genuine and -- well, are you now in a position to accept that those documents are genuine?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You must tell me what documents you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: My understanding is that you were given access to by the Court certain challenged documents, because I checked that last week and I understood you were -- had already been provided with them. Do you remember the documents with which you were provided?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now things are clearer, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, have you been able to check on the -- on those documents?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on the last day of my testimony I did manage to contact certain persons in the Ministry of the Interior, and on that day I sent them a fax of the documents that I took over, and I have information as of yesterday that during the course of the day today I would be receiving certain information with respect to three written documents which I sent out to them. I do believe that the Tribunal knows and that you know that with respect to the photograph and the individuals showed on the overhead projector, that steps have been taken --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'll come to that in a second. I want to deal with things separately. So that we can forecast receiving sometime today an answer by the government on the three documents that you forwarded to them that apparently reveal the presence of MUP or Skorpions at the area of Srebrenica in the July of 1995.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not question, Mr. Prosecutor, the presence of the Skorpions that you showed in Srebrenica. All I am challenging is, and I'm definitely challenging that, that they belonged to the sector of public security. Now, whether they belonged to some other sector of the Ministry of the Interior I said that I had absolutely no knowledge of any of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, staying with the documents, we're not thinking about or talking about the video yet, is your answer that you do not question the presence of Skorpions in Srebrenica, is that different from or the same as the evidence you gave last week?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not bringing into question the presence of those persons from the photograph at the location that we saw, but I did not see nor do I have any proof or evidence that it was indeed those --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Sorry if my questions aren't clear but I'm going to keep you on the track I wish, if you would be so good. You were asked, before you were shown the video, questions about documents. The documents showed the presence of Skorpions or MUP in Srebrenica. You challenged those documents. And unless my recollection is entirely false, you did not accept, on the basis of the documents, that Skorpions were present. Now, have you changed your mind? Have you changed your position, please? And, if so, why?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not in any sense changed my mind with respect to the fact that the Skorpions, according to your statement, belonged to the Ministry of the Interior. So in that sense, I have not changed my mind in any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I think you knew what I was getting at, Mr. Stevanovic. Have you changed your position on whether Skorpions were present in the Srebrenica in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me repeat: I do not exclude the possibility of the fact that members of that group were there, but I do exclude the possibility that they in any way belonged to the sector of public security of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: To that I will return. Now, let's turn to the second topic, the video. It may be everyone in court knows this, but for the sake of the record it's as well that I explain something you can confirm. Following the playing of a small part of the video here and the request to you to identify individuals, it happened that either a full version of what would appear to be the same tape or very much more, a very much longer version of the same tape, was played on television in Serbia; correct?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know that some of the tape was shown, but I don't know how much. I thought that what was shown there is the same footage that was shown here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And as a result of the showing of that footage in Serbia by an agency entirely different from the Office of the Prosecutor, nothing to do with us, victims were identified and perpetrators or alleged perpetrators were arrested, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have that information from the information media in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And as many as ten people were arrested within hours, four of them being -- I think something like four of them being detained in custody.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have information about the first part of your observation, that eight to ten alleged members of the unit that were shown on the footage were arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Help me as a former active policeman and present employee of the MUP: How was it possible, do you know, for these men who you say had nothing to do with the MUP to be arrested within hours of that broadcast of a larger portion of the tape?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is difficult to answer that question, but I have given it a great deal of thought about everything that happened here, and it is quite certain that while I was an active duty assistant minister of the interior that had we had footage of that kind we would have taken urgent measures to uncover those individuals and arrest them, and I do believe that the Ministry of the Interior, starting out from the video footage and probably because they had some information before that, reacted in the way they did; urgently. And that is quite normal and natural for that kind of reaction faced with a case of that kind. The only question is whether the results are good enough, and I think that at this point in time they indeed are.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Do you now accept that the video we saw last week in part and of which you have had the photographs and names provided, or proposed names provided, do you now accept that that shows a group known as the Skorpions killing people taken from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have any reason to doubt what you said and what you showed us. I, of course, really did not see any insignia or signs there on the basis of which I would be able to claim that it was that particular group, but I believe what you said, and I believe what you showed. But I continue to maintain that they certainly did not belong to the Ministry of the Interior or, rather, specifically, the public security sector of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Very well. As a result of having the stills from the video with the proposed names, have you been able to make any inquiries so as to tell us one way or another whether the names provided to you were or were not members of the MUP at the time?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The names from the video and the stills I did not send to Belgrade because before I decided to send them I received information that the group had already been arrested. So my interests with regard to the group, despite the obligation that I took upon myself, would not have been professionally in proper order because in a way I could have influenced steps with respect to the investigation. I assume that you will be able to receive that information from the ministry. Very simply, I decided on three documents containing the 11 names that we discussed that I send that out and during the course of the day today I expect to receive feedback information as to what has been asserted up until now, and when I do receive that information I will send it in to the Registry or the people in the Registry in the Tribunal who communicate with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Turn to your suggestion that the Skorpions were not subordinated to the MUP. Will you take, please, tab 151 in volume 4. This is a document for which we do have a translation, and to remind the Court, if we look at the English translation and if the witness looks at the original for tab 151, we'll see this relates to crime reported by an employee of the Podujevo OUP which is -- OUP is still part of the MUP, isn't it, Mr. Stevanovic?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is part of the Secretariat of the Interior in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And of course the Ministry of the Interior as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: So this person reported several bodies in Rahmana Morine Street. There was on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I do know about that case.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Nineteen bodies, and included amongst them children, women, and so on. And we see at the bottom that the criminal report was submitted for this incident against known perpetrators Sasa Cvjetan and Dejan Demirovic; correct?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've already said that during the examination so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And these men were shown to be members of the reserve force of the Republic of Serbia, SAJ, and without any doubt that is a unit that is under your part of the police, as you confirmed that last week.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. It is a unit which came under the public security sector. At one period of time it was outside the sector, but I think during the period -- the material time it was within the sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, just give me a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Now, these men were two of the men eventually prosecuted for crimes, and I'm going to look at the overall statistics for prosecutions with you a little later. I'm dealing with this point now because of its connection to Skorpions.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I also, in reading the papers yesterday, heard that these people who were arrested and against whom a criminal report was filed do have something to do with the Skorpions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: All right. Which people arrested?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the two men against whom the criminal report was filed, who had been arrested previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You're ahead of me, aren't you, Mr. Stevanovic, because you know that your account of Skorpions not being subordinated is dishonest, and you're leading with a defence to what you know is coming.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true. All I'm doing is --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: What did you do over the weekend, pray help us, that suddenly drew to your attention that these two men, Cvjetan and his colleague, clearly subordinated to the MUP through the SAJ, were also connected to the Skorpions? What is it that drew that to your attention over the weekend?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's quite simple. I read the papers. I have them in my room. I can bring them in here. And I didn't read any documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Which paper of yours shows, please, that Cvjetan and his colleague were members of Skorpions? We see from your papers that they were members of reserve MUP and SAJ -- or subordinated to the SAJ, but which document shows they were Skorpions?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what I want to explain to you. I said quite clearly that from the information media, I learnt that these people had something to do with the Skorpions, but of course I didn't explain the rest. You have to ask me or you have to give me more time to answer. As I was saying, I received information that they did have something to do. At that point in time I cannot confirm or refute that information, but I still stand by --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you can help us as much as you can, but we're going to look at it logically. So --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: -- "information media" and "I received information." I want you to tell us precisely what you received over the weekend that told you that these men were members of the Skorpions.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can do is to bring in the papers that I read you. I'm talking about the news where there is sporadic mention of the fact that these two men against whom a criminal report was filed belonged to the Skorpions. I claim, and I still claim, everything that I said before; that these two men belonged to the reserve force of the special anti-terrorist unit and they could not have belonged to any kind of paramilitary group. They were only as individuals members of the reserve force of that unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: General --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And quite possibly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What was the date of the report that you read? When was that newspaper published?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is yesterday's papers or the day before. They are papers in Serbian, and they carry certain comments in Serbia with respect to the events we saw on the footage. And with respect to those events, they bring that group in connection with this crime that we have a document on here and the case here in the tab before us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm not in a position to accept or reject at the moment, although I will of course check it, I'm not in a position to accept or reject whether newspapers over this last weekend revived memories of the trial of Cvjetan and his colleague showing them to be Skorpions, but we will now look at two short contemporary records of their trial. If we can make these available, please, from Vreme. This is from Vreme on the 25th of December, 2003, and two passages translated. The first passage I'd like you to look at can be found on page 24 at the bottom, as it's given, 25. Thank you. And it reads as follows: "The crime on 7 Rahmana Morine Street, occurred on March 28th, 1999, only four days after the ... bombing... That day, a group of Special Forces - Skorpions (compiled from veterans from the wars in Bosnia and Croatia) as part of the SAJ ... was directed towards the city." It goes on, does the report, to say: "Even though the court is still deciding over the specific of what really happened after the Skorpions entered Podujevo, today the following is clear: Commander of the unit, Slobodan Medic Boca, left for a meeting in the town, and he ordered his soldiers to wait in the buses until he came back, yet the soldiers did not listen to him, they left the buses in groups and they dispersed around the surrounding houses, apparently looking for a place to stay, however, in their apparent search for a place to stay, they also robbed stores, searched citizens who they met on the streets, or within their homes, took their belongings ... Soon after one of the Skorpion groups entered a house full of civilians on Rahmana Morine Street, gunshots was heard, and in the yard of the house there was a pile of bodies in the courtyard. Immediately following the incident, Commander Boca arrived and spoke '... I cannot even leave you for a minute without Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. you --'" and his view is expressed in vulgar terms. "He ordered the Skorpions back onto the buses, while one of the units was returned to Serbia ..." Does that accord with your recollection of how the trial was presented against the two men?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not have any recollection of what happened at the trial of these people. Some of the elements and details here can be read in the newspapers, and since you're interested, I'm going to bring in the newspaper that I read and then you'll be able to see that what I'm telling you is quite correct. But let me put it this way: I never had, up until yesterday, information that there was a group of Skorpions over there. I never until yesterday, or the day before, rather, had any knowledge of the fact that Boca was there, but what I want to state here, if you allow me, of course, some important things, because I'm worried that if I answer briefly I'm not going to be able to give you all the important information I wish to give you. It is a question of the reserve force, and within the force -- they can be included in the police force as individuals. At this point in time, I don't wish to challenge the possibility that after the war, in 1996, somebody, some of the members of those units, did join the reserve force pursuant to the provisions and law governing those -- that procedure. But I claim at that time within the ministry there could not have been any alien foreign unit from any previous war as a formation, as a unit per se. Some members of different formations and units, individuals, could have joined the reserve police force, or any unit, and that question is settled at a tactical level, decided at a tactical level. It is not a question which is decided upon at a medium level and particularly not a strategic level. Of course at this point in time let me repeat: I cannot confirm or refute that. These are newspaper articles. There is no reason for me to doubt them but I do doubt quite certainly that they weren't interpreted -- the facts weren't interpreted in the proper way, although we can see clearly here we're dealing with a reserve force, and let me repeat: You cannot have a unit join a reserve force. You can have individuals join reserve forces if they fulfil provisions and conditions provided by law. If a unit were -- could enter, I don't know of any case like that where a unit became part of the reserve force.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If I cut you too short too early you must ask for leave to conclude.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: But two immediate points arise before we press on. We're going to discover that it was about two or three, four or five or six MUP policemen in all prosecuted for anything. You, in 1999, were in charge in Kosovo to a large degree, and you're still in the MUP in 2003 when this trial happened. Are you telling us the truth when you say you have no recollection of this trial of people said to be subordinated to the SAJ committing these appalling crimes? Are you saying you have no recollection of that crime until the weekend? I see.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely that's not what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... in 2003, not looking at television, not reading newspapers, not talking to your colleagues? How could you be so ignorant, Mr. Stevanovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, the transcript says, "Absolutely that's not what I'm saying," so I'm a bit confused about the answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did you have any knowledge of this trial -- do you have any recollection of this trial until you read newspapers over the weekend?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I'm familiar with the trial. I have said that the trial is under way in Serbia. On one of the earlier days I said that. But you are suggesting an answer to me to confuse me. I said several times that I know about these events ever since it happened. I know that the same minute the members of the group who were suspected of committing this act were returned to Serbia. The same minute. And I said the investigation started immediately. It was conducted urgently. The criminal report was filed several days later. Perpetrators were identified several days later. They were arrested in Novi Sad. Mr. Prosecutor, to me as assistant minister, those issues were of interest. As assistant minister I cannot deal with the CVs of 25.000 policemen and several thousand reservists. So I do not know their CVs, but I know everything that is written in the criminal report and I followed the trial, but I claim still that I did not make the link between the accused and the Skorpions. I have already said all of this at least twice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I ask a question here, Mr. Nice, or would that be disturbing the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No, not at all, Your Honour. I'll be only too happy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Does it follow from that, Mr. Stevanovic, that your understanding was that these officers who were arrested were part of the public security section of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And does it also follow from that that Boca was therefore part of the public security section of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That obviously follows if he was there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Okay. And does it therefore also follow that the public security sector of the MUP were responsible for what would appear to have been a massacre in Rahmana Morine Street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is not in dispute. That massacre was perpetrated by members of the public security of the MUP of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: We've had evidence in this Court from a man called Milan Milanovic or Mrgud, and I believe it was all in open session and I'll be corrected if any part of it was not, revealing that Medic agreed in answer to a request for troops to go to Kosovo in early 1999 with some 150 men from Novi Sad. Do you remember that happening?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I absolutely don't remember. I don't remember any discussions with that Mr. Medic. I told you when I saw him on what occasion and for what reason. I don't know where he was later, nor did I have any contact nor do I know that anybody from the MUP was in touch with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: How could it be, with you in your very senior position and your -- with your -- with access to the information at the meetings you attended, how could it be that 150 men under Medic, a very well-known man, could be sent to help in Kosovo without your knowing? How could that happen?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If 150 men were -- from such a group were really sent to Kosovo, then it would be really incredible for me not to know but you may rest assured that I really don't know. First of all, I don't know that 150 men were sent. All I know is what is written in the criminal report and partially what you've just read, but I don't know the link between the perpetrators of this crime and the Skorpions group.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, do you remember this, then: That after the commission of this appalling crime the Medic group was withdrawn from Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know very well that a group of reservists of a special anti-terrorist unit which was suspected at the time of committing this crime was returned from Kosovo the same moment, the same moment, literally half an hour later. We were all informed about this, and our unanimous position was that the suspects have to be returned from Kosovo immediately and an investigation started, and that's what happened. And in my opinion, that was the important thing; to prevent further crimes, to identify perpetrators, to file a criminal report, for them to be arrested, and that was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... please, this, the most -- what role did General Vlastimir Djordjevic hold in Kosovo in the period of March to June of 1999?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He remained in his position. He used to be head of the public security sector, and he's had the normal powers that you have in peacetime --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- as head of that sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Was he subordinate to you, parallel to you, superior to you? Help us.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was not subordinate to me. But at that time, you could say that he was not my superior either. We were both in the public security sector but we were both assistant ministers. And in 1998 and 1999, I received my orders directly from the minister and so did he. So you could say that we were both in parallel subordinated to the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did you and Djordjevic trust each other?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in principle, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did he ever keep things from you, General Djordjevic?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I don't know whether he kept anything from me. All I know is what he told me. I don't know if there is anything that he didn't tell me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Because you would need to know --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's always probably something that people don't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: There could be no reason for Djordjevic to keep back from you his access to reinforcements or his deployment of reinforcements in Kosovo, could there?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think he kept back anything. Reinforcements for Kosovo were a matter of course. I cannot claim that I knew everything, but I knew, generally speaking, all about reinforcements and withdrawals from Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... with this: The same witness tells us that a couple of weeks after the Skorpions were withdrawn, Djordjevic had them brought back. What do you say to that? It can be found on transcript pages 27830, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that. I know very well, though, that several police units were in Kosovo at the time, all special units, the special anti-terrorist unit, and the SAJ. So if anyone from the reserve force of the special anti-terrorist unit was in Kosovo, that would have been normal. But I don't know that anyone from the Skorpions group was brought back to Kosovo because, and I'm saying this again, if in a special unit there was a reservist who was a member of the Skorpions from the Republic of Serbian Krajina, then it might have been only a result of his selection in keeping with the regular procedure, but the whole unit could not have been made part of the reserve force. The reserve force is a combination of individuals, not units. For them to be returned to Kosovo the decision of the minister would have been necessary, and I don't know about any such decision of the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Could we have a private session for a couple of minutes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can we please then look, the last point, the same article detailing the trial of Cvjetan, which is at page 25 for you, "The Guardians of the Oil," where Medic gave an account. See whether this helps you at all one way or the other. "Slobodan Medic Boca, commander of Skorpions, spoke in the court about the history of his unit, but his statements on that subject sometimes were somewhat different. During the court appearance on the 28th of March, 2003, he stated: 'The Skorpion units were formed in 1991 as part of the Yugoslav army (sic!) as a regular unit. They operated in the region of Bosnia and Croatia. After the end of war operations in Bosnia and Croatia, they were transferred to Serbia and the men discharged. The core of the unit was preserved in accordance to the rules and in accordance to the instructions we received in order to provide that the men could have a normal life.' A few months later, on December the 5th, Commander Boca replied to the same question with the following answer: 'The Skorpion units were created on May 1992 in order to protect "Oil Industries of Krajina" and they stayed in that capacity from 1992-1996. Afterwards, because I demanded that my unit be part of MUP Serbia, the Skorpions became part of the reserve composition of Special Anti-terrorist Units of MUP Serbia.' By the way, it is well known that oil wells in East Slavonia were quite profitable source of income for the president of RSK Goran Hadzic and the deceased ... Arkan." Are you in a position to help us with any part of what Medic said, as to whether it's either true or false? First of all, the history of being part of the army. Do you remember its being part of the army?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only repeat what I have already said: All I know about them I know because in 1995, in the second half of 1995, I visited Eastern Slavonia. I ran into the man by accident two or three times maybe, and I believed then that they belonged to the army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina or perhaps the police. I don't know any of the rest. I don't know when they were established, what he was doing. I don't know what happened with them after the withdrawal from -- of the army and the police from Eastern Slavonia. I don't know that he asked to be admitted into the reserve force of the MUP of Serbia. I don't know whether any of them were indeed transferred or admitted, but it seems incredible to me that they could have been admitted as a unit. It is something not envisaged by the law. Not even the head of the sector could have made a decision to allow them to do that. And of course the minister can decide such things and doesn't have to inform me, but I would normally know about such a decision because such a decision would be against the law. The law says that an individual who meets the requirements may be admitted into the reserve force, and that is done at the level of every unit. In order to admit an individual, a high level decision is not necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: My final suggestion to you on the Skorpions and Slobodan Medic certainly at this stage is that, Mr. Stevanovic, you have been less than frank with this Court from the first time I mentioned the Skorpions and Medic, and you have been forced to make such concessions as you have by evidence that you see to be irresistible. Isn't that the truth?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct, Mr. Prosecutor. You seem to be linking me with everything bad that happened in the territory of the former Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Yugoslavia. I would really appreciate it if you would spare me from such qualifications. And I'm telling you, I have nothing to do with the Skorpions, and I know with the passage of time that will become clear, and I will still be here and we can confront this again. I understand you need to compromise me, and I understand the position of this Court, but I would really hate it to be put into -- to be linked with everything evil and bad that happened in the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I must turn to another topic, and the topics won't be in particular order but they have to be taken in the order I take them for various reasons, and I'm going to turn to Racak. If Mr. Nort would be good enough to get the plans lying on the wall over there. It may need an easel. And we'll turn briefly to Racak. You explained to us last week that you had basically no detailed knowledge of Racak at all. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have explained already that I wasn't there on the spot. I really never went to Racak. I also explained that at the time of the event, I wasn't in Kosovo, I was in Belgrade, and most of my information comes from official documentation and from reports received by the ministry from the staff in the SUP in Urosevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Even on the basis of having read the material, you had limited knowledge of what happened at Racak, as I understood it; correct?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that I did not have complete information. Of course I would have had more information had I been there, but I read the case file on Racak and I have seen most of the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And you understood those who died to have died -- are said to have been attacked as a group or to have been attacking as a group and been defeated as a group, with their weapons taken from them where they fell. Would that be about right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I didn't understand that they were attacked, and I have tried to explain what my understanding was several times. The police were attacked from Racak when they tried to perform their legitimate job and achieve a legitimate goal. It is because of the attack from Racak that armed combat ensued. All that I know about it indicates that all those who died died because of the legitimate use of weapons by the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Now, because you weren't able to help us with the plan, I'm showing for you, and you can take a moment or so to familiarise yourself with it, an aerial which has been marked. I -- don't worry too much with the English on the left. I'll interpret that for you as necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If the camera could possibly be focused on the plan, I'd be grateful because I can't see it quite well enough from this distance to read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Are you aware yourself at all as to where the main body of dead people were found, Mr. Stevanovic?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly all the locations where bodies were found, but I remember the scenes from the mosque where the bodies were gathered, and I remember part of the external examination and maybe part of the post-mortem was performed, but I don't know where the bodies were before the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If you look at the map before you, number 5, which you can see there, marks what's called a gully where a very large number of people were found dead, 20. Did you know about 20 people or did your reading lead you to learn about 20-odd people found dead in a gully?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember some photographs related to that gully.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Here's two photographs I'd like you to look at. We'll place on the overhead projector. Just lay these two photographs on the overhead projector, please. First of all, these are from Exhibit 156, tab 5. These, you see -- we can now put first of all the first photograph on the overhead projector. Look at that. That shows one of the bodies found in the gully. Next photograph, Mr. Nort. That shows the head of the same body with the bullet wound beside the neck. Do you have enough experience as a policeman to know what that sort of wound indicates?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you something, but with a reservation that I'm not an expert pathologist and that I'm not a criminal investigation policeman; I'm a policeman in general terms. The general comment I would make is that this is an exit and -- entry and exit wound, and all I know about such traces is what I learnt at criminology classes at school --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- but I cannot tell you anything further about what that means.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm only going to ask you a few questions to see if you can help us. If you'd look on the map again, if we could see that. You'll see that -- you'll see round and about number 5 there are lots of other places marked. You can see 4, 3, 2, 1. And you will know from the area that the distances between 4 and 5 or 3 and 5 is quite substantial. We're not dealing with a few metres, we're dealing with considerable distances. And so can you find the one that -- see number 3 and 3/7? Can we just lay these three documents on the overhead projector so that you can understand the evidence before I ask you a question. First of all, the title page, please, Mr. Nort for scene 3/7. This is direction of travel of the victims and the witness pointing to the areas where three Mehmetis, one aged 22, one aged 54 -- sorry, two Mehmetis were killed. That's father and brother. Father and daughter, I beg your pardon. I'm grateful. Now, let's look at the first photograph, please. This shows the surviving son who was injured and could have been seen in a hospital to be spoken to, pointing to where his father and sister was killed. Next photograph, please. And another view of the same. Now, if you look at that location on 3/5, you've got your thing pointed on it, help me with this: From all the materials that the accused wants you to put into evidence and that therefore I assume you're familiar with, is there any document that shows that weapons in the hands of the man and his daughter who died there were collected from that place?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I cannot answer this question because I have no knowledge about this whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Stevanovic. Your -- the invitation, which I'm resisting, is that the Court should accept 140 documents analysing the Racak incident. My search, and earnest search, is to find material that shows in any way the recovery of weapons from these locations away from location number 5. Here is a location where a man and his daughter were shot and where the son was injured. It's your material. It's not my material. You're bringing it in. Is there any material anywhere that shows that weapons were recovered from these out -- these distant places where people died? Please help us.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can help you in the following way: It is quite certain that in the village of Racak there was fighting. There's no doubt about that. Of course the reason for the fighting is the attack that came from Racak that was launched against the police unit that had as its task to search for the terrorists and find them. I cannot testify in any great detail. I cannot testify about how a particular person was killed or whether that particular person had weapons or not. You know and I know, of course, that in relation to the investigation and other things that were supposed to be carried out after the event itself there were quite a few problems. I know that the bodies had been moved, that the unit did not stay there overnight to secure the crime scene because of the danger of being attacked. So I really am not a witness who can talk about minutiae of that kind that are yet very important, and you insisted on that in your last question. That is a matter for detailed and long investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stevanovic, at every possible point in your evidence-in-chief to this accused, when asked about any crime site, you gave answers that exculpated him and the Serbs. You do it on the basis of documents you say you have examined, and I am unapologetic about seeking your detailed help, for if you can't help us on the accused's behalf, I don't know who can, you see. Perhaps have a look at two more, and we'll look at this one. Find on the map crime location 4, scene 9.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume, Mr. Prosecutor, that this question is structured along similar lines as the previous one was. If I'm supposed to answer what happened at a specific point in time at a specific place, then for me that is a question that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Wait for --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Now, if Mr. Nort would show on the overhead projector, you having seen where crime scene 4/9 is, now please look at the photographs in order. First of all the title page. Yes, leave the title page there. This is crime location 4, scene 9, photographs showing the direction to and the areas where three people were found, one aged 21, one aged 14, and one aged 54. Next photograph, please. Here we see a map showing where that location is aerially viewed, at the end of an intended escape route. Next photograph, please. This shows the three deceased clearly moved from where they died to inside a house nearby, but it shows them. The 14-year-old boy and the two others. Now, looking -- and last photograph, please, Mr. Nort. That's the father with his walking stick, as you see. I'm going to ask you two questions about this part of the scene that you've brought evidence about. First, the same first question: Do you -- can you point me in your materials to any piece of paper that shows the recovery of weapons from roughly the area of scene 4/9 where these three people died?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that as for these tabs, there is not a single document that would show that weapons were found on a particular person. As far as I can recall, at the moment of the on-site investigation weapons were found in one particular location or a few, due to the fact that the police had left the scene. I brought the documents that could have been compiled at the time when they were compiled. The documents were compiled sometime after the actual events and sometime after the situation on the scene itself had been changed. All my information indicates that it was not the police that changed the situation on the scene but it was the villagers who did it or the terrorists, depending on what would be proven to be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: All your information indicates that. Well, you better tell us what it is, then. What is this information that shows the villagers had changed the scene? If you want to say that, make it good.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only know about that from information from documents that I read or from the oral information I had from persons who were in charge of that sector. I think that documents also indicate that fact, that is to say that at least for one night the scene had not been under the control of the police. That is the knowledge I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Absolutely correct. Now, go -- but before you slur, if it is a slur, the relations of those who died, I want you to make good your observation that it wasn't the police that changed the situation on the scene but the villagers who did it or the terrorists. I want you to make that good.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course what I can prove to you is my own knowledge about that, the knowledge I have from the documents that are presented here. I repeat: I was not an eyewitness. I cannot, therefore, say to you that the situation had been changed by the police or by the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Don't hold back. Tell us everything you were told by local people, point us to every document to show that this scene was corrupted by the bereaved and/or by the terrorists.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, the knowledge I have is that during one of the continuations of the on-site investigation the bodies were found in the mosque. I really cannot imagine any logical version that would involve the police collecting the bodies and putting them into the mosque when the danger was there of continued fighting and when the police had to withdraw from the site.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Absolutely right and everybody agrees that the bodies were recovered. But that's not what you're saying. You're suggesting there was some misrepresentation of where the bodies might have been found. I want you to make that good.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Please, that's not what I said at all. I made a general statement that when the fighting stopped and all the way up to the arrival of the police investigation organs on the scene the situation on the scene had been changed in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Would you like to turn to the map this time and look to crime location 2, scene 2, and we'll all see that displayed with the audiovisual booth's assistance, if we could have a look at the map. Crime location 2, there we see it, scene 2. Still some considerable distance from number 5, the gully. Mr. Nort, if you'd now be good enough to display on the overhead projector the title page. This is 2/2, photograph showing the direction from the village to and the areas where three men, 60, 62, and 58, were killed. And let's take the first photograph, please. Now, these three brothers who you see lying there in the area of I think their home but I'm not sure of that, the same question again: Any material in the papers that can explain who, when, and how their weapons were removed from this scene?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite certainly there is no fact that can be ascertained in terms of who took what weapon from what individual. Could you please be so kind as to tell me the origin of these photographs? Were these taken by the police or by who? I do not recall having seen this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: These were taken by OSCE on the first arrival of the international presence there, by a witness who has been called before this Court.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's finally now that Mr. Nice explained to the witness what kind of exhibits these are. He's bringing into question the documents that are very voluminous, that pertain to Racak, and that General Stevanovic testified about. And then, while bringing that into question, he is not showing him exhibits that have to do with his testimony. He's showing him his own exhibits, and General Stevanovic is not testifying about that. I don't think that that is proper to challenge things in that way during the cross-examination, to challenge something that the witness did not even speak about at all. The witness did not speak about the exhibits that Mr. Nice has, he spoke about the documents that the police had, and he's asking him to explain his exhibits. How can General Stevanovic explain Mr. Nice's exhibits?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, the Prosecutor is entitled in cross-examination to put an exhibit to the witness notwithstanding that it wasn't put in chief. If there is a problem with the authenticity, the source of the witness, then that is a matter that can be raised either by the witness or by yourself. Proceed, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Mr. Stevanovic, you have heard the accused's observations. You will have heard me ask you half a dozen times in the last 15 minutes to point us to any exhibit in the pile of exhibits that the accused wants to produce through you that deals with the issues I raise. Are there any documents in the exhibits you produce or, rather, that the accused wishes to produce through you that deal with the issues I've raised? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really looked at all the documents that were put into several tabs and that have to do with Racak. These are documents that the police and the investigative judge in charge prepared, and those are the documents that I had occasion to see. I did not have an opportunity to see the photographs that were made by someone else. Possibly I saw them on television without knowing whose photographs they were. Of course, according to what I know and according to what exists in the Ministry of Interior, I said what I said and I brought here, that is contained in the binders, in the documents, a series of documents in terms of what I said. As for the details of the event itself, I repeat once again, and the events at the microlocations, I really do not know about the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You remember that we -- you were asked a question, I think by His Honour Judge Bonomy in respect of Racak, Is there a statement from the man in charge of the exercise? You were asked a similar question by me. It was made clear to you that you were the policeman, whether just public or public and secret is another matter, but you were the policeman dealing with all crime sites. I don't have anybody else to ask apart from you. That's why I'm asking you these questions. Do you understand that? All right. Mr. Nort, the next picture, please, or the next --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to answer, of course. I could give answers to questions about which I have knowledge. Regrettably, as a rule you put questions to me about which I know less, but that's simply the way it is. Had you asked me about details about which I do know, of course my questions [as interpreted] would have been positive for the most part. Since your questions are such that you are basically asking me about microdetails which, I repeat, are very important, it is only natural that I, generally speaking, give negative answers because I was not there. I was not an eyewitness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm still going to ask you a few more questions and then we'll move on, but this photograph here has white and blue markers. On the evidence, the white markers are the bodies and the blue markers are the bullets or are bullets. You see? It may be suggested, I don't know if this is your suggestion, that the bodies were redistributed around the area of Racak after they died somewhere else. Is there any document in -- that you can turn us to or any piece of information or any bit of hearsay that a villager gave to you, anything you like, Mr. Stevanovic, that could explain how it is that these three men, 58 to 60, are lying where they are with bullets in the appropriate location with no evidence of weapons being taken from the three brothers? Is there anything that can explain that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, my answer will be similar to the previous answers I gave. First of all, I don't know whether weapons were found or not as regards these three particular casualties. Secondly, I don't know whether they were moved or not in relation to the specific microlocation. I know, generally speaking, that when the -- after the on-site investigation had started, the scene had been changed significantly, because most of the victims happened to be later in the mosque, which is in the village, in the centre of the village, wherever.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: My last question on this type relates -- if Mr. Nort will be good enough, and we'll move on to another issue. 156, tab 12. Just lay that on the overhead projector, please. We're now back, Mr. Stevanovic, to the gully where the large majority of people were found, and European Union expert team -- the colours aren't showing very well, at least not on my monitor but I hope they're sufficient -- discovered bullets and bullet casings at the scene of the gully, the black numbers referring to various bodies that were found there. Do you follow?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The blue, almost all in the gully or thereabouts, are bullets. The red are bullet casings. Now, you've had a lot of experience in Kosovo, as you tell us. You were in charge of special units in Croatia, and you were the senior officer in the Bosnian borders, so you had a lot of experience of this war. Does that distribution of bullet casings and bullets and dead men suggest an execution to you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Nice put that kind of question to Professor Dobricanin, who is a forensic expert, and the answer he got is that is impossible because of the bullet path direction. I think that it is pointless to put this kind of question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, if the witness cannot answer the question, he's competent to say so. Are you in a position to answer the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I really am not a forensic expert or a ballistics expert. As the Prosecutor said, I did not have any experience from combat. I did not take part in any combat, and I never analysed the traces of the projectile, the place where the casings are, the place where the casualties were, et cetera. I can talk about that as someone who is a bit in a better position than a pure layman, because I have graduated from the military academy after all, but I really cannot give you a qualified answer to any one of these questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Last question on this document: If the men in the gully died where they fell and if they were firing back, you would expect to find shell casings from their guns in their positions. Is there any document that you know of in the material that you've produced that explains why no such shell casings were found?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, I can agree with the first statement you made, but I repeat: The police did not carry out an on-site investigation immediately after the event concerned and at the moment when the victims were in the place where they got killed. Obviously you made a considerable effort to do this and to have your concept of this. This is the first time I see this picture. In order to give any kind of answer, I would have to give it a great deal of thought and I'd have to consult and so on and so forth. A lot of things could have happened within a single hour on the scene, not to mention all the things that could happen within one year or even more than that. One of the axioms of criminal investigations is that nothing should be changed on the site itself so that the investigation could start on a stable basis. Regrettably, what happened here happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You've never considered the forensic scientific evidence, the evidence of photographs, and all the other material available to this Court, have you?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have seen what is contained in the tabs that are here right next to me. As for the other exhibits you have, I have not seen them except for those that you showed me during these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Now, as to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Nort. I think that's ...

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: As to the identity of the victims, what can you help us with so far as that's concerned? What sort of victims were they?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, a vast majority of the victims were men. I seem to remember only one woman and one child. I don't think there were more persons who belonged to those categories. There were persons belonging to different age groups, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And as to the suggestion that the victims were either civilians or members of the KLA or fighting members of the KLA, how can you help us, please?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All my knowledge indicates that these are persons who were engaged in fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Detail, please. All your knowledge.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, in fighting there can be collateral consequences as well. I haven't got any details. I really have not got any details.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: All your knowledge, can you -- if you want to say things like that, can you explain why? Why do you say these people were KLA?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I say that on the basis of the information that I believed and that I believe now, too, on the basis of the information received from the persons in charge of the territory of Racak and on the basis of the documents that I read, that I familiarised myself with, and that are contained here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Generalities aren't going to help us assess your evidence, Mr. Stevanovic. Who spoke to you and told you they were KLA? Which documents have you relied on? Point us to them.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an attack on the police using firearms. It is quite certain that civilians would not attack the police using firearms. That would be an extreme case. But if that happens where the KLA headquarters is anyway, anybody who attacks the police, it is only logical, would have to belong to that group, that formation. There can be some exceptions, though, and of course the consequences may perhaps be broader than consequences sustained by the terrorists only. When there is fighting in an area that is so close to residential areas, that kind of possibility cannot be precluded altogether.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You know there's no statement in all the papers from the man who led the operation for the Serb police, so can you point me to any other statement, written statement, or you can tell us what you were told by one of policemen. Go on, tell us what you were told or what you read.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this documentation, indeed there is no statement of the person who led the operation itself. We have stated that several times now. But there is a report that includes that kind of information too. Of course that does not mean that a witness will not come here, as you said awhile ago, who would bring all of this and who will be an eyewitness who will testify to all of that. I can only testify to what I know, and I can only tell you about things I know. You keep insisting that I should talk about the situation on the ground, and it is general knowledge by now that I was not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, within the papers you've produced, is there any particular category of document that you rely on to show that these victims were actually members of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I used documents that we quoted in part during my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, what were they? You tell us.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already mentioned one of them. That is the report that we quoted in part. Then there is the record of the on-site investigation. It is the entire documentation contained in these tabs. We can have a look at it again now and analyse it again. You have to decide that. I cannot search for it through the tabs now and remember each and every individual document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to draw your attention to the following: The documents that have to do with Racak and that were tendered here during General Stevanovic's testimony are in 7, 8 and 9, tabs 7, 8 and 9. These are three tabs with a large number of documents. If Mr. Nice wants to ask him about some document, he has to indicate the document he has in mind. No one can expect the witness to know all those documents just off-the-cuff. They're right next to him. Show them to him. But this is not a fair way of dealing with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, if you have in mind a particular document from any of those tabs, then you can direct the witness to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If I chose to, Your Honour, but it's not my choice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Indeed, why should Mr. Nice direct the witness to documents that he is professing a knowledge of?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm grateful to Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm going to turn to -- that's all I'm going to ask specifically related to Racak, I think, for the time being, but I want to ask you one other question that may ultimately become associated, and it's this: As a senior policeman, if material's published going to show that one of your police stations is behaving improperly, what action would you take?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whenever knowledge reaches me that any policeman, and especially a whole police unit, is behaving unlawfully, according to the rules the leader of that station is informed about the report coming in, and he is required to report on it. If the complaint is of a more serious nature, then as a rule a group is set up at a higher level which is given the assignment of looking into the matter, checking everything out, and talking to the person submitting the criminal report, talking and interviewing the people concerned --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I don't know whether --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it's a convenient time. We'll take a break for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Before I return to where I was, so as not to overlook something, I should tell the Court that we have identified a newspaper article this morning - today is the 6th of June, is it not? - referring to the sitting of the Skorpions trial of the -- or the trial of the Skorpion Cvjetan, resumption of the trial. It doesn't in any sense change my position vis-a-vis this witness, but it is true that the matter was referred to in Serbian newspaper today.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I return to where we were. Would you look, please, at this document, which is not yet an exhibit. One for the overhead projector because it's in English and it's not in. One for the accused. One for the accused and then we'll deal with the overhead projector. It's in English, Mr. Stevanovic, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No, Mr. Nort. One for the accused. Thank you. And one for the overhead projector. If we could go to the last page but one, Mr. Nort. It's got 31 on the bottom right-hand corner, so that we can just see what it says there. 31, bottom right-hand corner. Second to last page. Thank you. You were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: This is a document, right at the bottom under "Note." Right. "This Spotlight --" thank you very much. "This Spotlight Report," says the document, Kosovo Albanians, it has been sent to the parliament, government, Ministry of the Interior, Ministry of Justice, prosecutor's office, and the president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, and to the same institutions of the Republic of Serbia. "The report is being sent to the United Nations General Assembly, Security Council," et cetera, et cetera. This is a report prepared by the Humanitarian Law Centre, of which we've spoken earlier. And if we come back to the front page, please, Mr. Nort, you will see what that says about it. It's report number 16, "Kosovo Albanians," dated February 1995. Were you aware personally of the receipt of this document by the organs of government referred to?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is the first time that I see a report with this title page, cover page, and I don't know that it was sent to anybody, but of course I have no --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You have no reason to doubt, do you, that the Humanitarian Law Centre, whose aim is to publicise wrongdoing and get action taken, would have sent this document to the organs of government identified. You have no reason to doubt that, do you?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, I do not, but I don't have any knowledge as to whether it was actually sent or not.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Might the volume of the interpretation be put up, please, for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Mr. Nort, if we could turn, please, to the bottom right-hand corner of page 15 and we'll rapidly turn to page 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: This report, you see, Mr. Stevanovic, sent as it suggests to all Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the organs of government - right at the bottom of the page, please - says under 3.3 this: "Electric shock at the Urosevac police station." And it reads: "FE, an 18-year-old, lives with his mother and younger brothers. On the morning of 11 April 1994, he was awakened by the doorbell. Before --" Over the page, please. "Before he could get dressed and downstairs, the police were already in the house. They had broken the glass in the front door and entered. They spoke Serbian, but when FE said he didn't understand, they switched to Albanian. They asked for and took his passport and driver's licence. They said they knew he was hiding weapons and would search the house. They looked under FE's bed, nothing more, and then took him with them to the police station. "They made me take off my shoes and sit on the floor. Two of them sat on my legs and asked if I had guns. 'No,' I answered, and the two of them ten truncheons each to the soles of my feet. They asked again. I answered the same. Again, ten blows from each. Then it was that they'd kill my mother if I don't tell them where my guns are. I said nothing. For the third time, ten blows from each. A total of 30 blows on each sole. They pulled me up on my feet, leaned me against a wall, boxed my head and ears, went at me with their truncheons until I was bleeding from the mouth. I fell, they pulled me up and again the same question. I answered they could do what they like, but I still had no guns. They ordered me to take off my pants. I was slow because of the pain, so they pulled them off. They tied my hands behind my back with my belt. They made me lay on the floor. I saw something that looked like a telephone. When I tried to get up, they pushed me down even harder. One held down my head and the other sat on my legs. They stuck wires from the apparatus that looked like a phone in my ears and on my sex organs. The pain was horrible. It was so terrible I lifted both of them, even though I was lying flat. When I screamed, they interrupted saying, 'Don't scream, it's disturbing.' They switched on the electricity three times. In between, they smoked cigarettes. They offered me one. While the electricity was on, they forced me to say, 'Hello,' 'I'll come tomorrow,' and similar nonsense. Finally, they told me to think it all over carefully and to bring in the guns in two days. They never mentioned what kind of guns. I had to hang on the fences to make it home." If true, a terrible indictment of that police station. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. If even part of this is true, then it's a terrible indictment of that police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: In light of what you said before the break, such information demands an inquiry by the police authorities, including yourself.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Information of this kind of course demands urgent inquiry and investigation on the part of the authorities of the MUP, but let me say that I really don't remember an event of this kind. That, of course, does not mean that it wasn't investigated and that the corresponding steps were not taken, but I really don't have any information about the event or whether any steps were taken by the police in that regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And -- you're ahead of me. I want you to take us to, point us to, tell us where we can find any investigation by your police of this allegation identifying as it should and could the policemen involved. Can you point me to where I can find such an investigation?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. The place to check out what was done pursuant to that information and whether the information was indeed sent to the Ministry of the Interior is the Ministry of the Interior of Serbia. I do not believe that it could happen that anybody in the Ministry of the Interior should receive information of this kind and not take urgent steps to check out the allegations.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The truth is that by 1995, Kosovo was a violent police state and allegations like this would simply be overlooked because they would be standard. Right or wrong.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Let me remind you, and let me explain why I probably didn't have information of that kind if it did reach the ministry at all. Let me remind you, as I was saying, that in 1995 and 1996 I spent time in Eastern Slavonia, and that was my assignment at that period. Of course, I didn't actually look at the date of the information, when it was sent to the ministry. I do not believe that it could happen that I don't know about this piece of information had it arrived in the ministry when I was in Belgrade. Quite possibly it arrived when I was not in Belgrade. But regardless of when it did actually arrive, I'm quite sure and certain that, having received information of this kind, all measures must have been taken to establish or challenge the truth of those allegations.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, I call for those documents if you're able to find them and provide them for us. Let me tell you something else: On the 22nd of May of 2002, three years ago, and at page 5554 to 5557 of the Court record, a witness gave an account not of being beaten himself but of seeing beatings by two police officers whom he named, a man called Jasovic and a man called Sparavalo. Do you know anything about those officers or nothing?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met Mr. Jasovic in The Hague while we were waiting to testify. Before that, I had not heard of either name.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You see, what this witness said well before the Defence case, well before any of the issues that you raise was that he saw a 50-year-old man Muhamed Bega from Ferizaj tied to a chair, handcuffed, and being beaten by those two officers. You know nothing to challenge the evidence of that witness, do you?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I don't know the testimony of the witness and then I don't know whether the witness did or did not tell the truth. For me to be able to say anything about any specific event and concrete information, I would have to know the contents of the information and to try to remember whether I know anything about it. Perhaps it would be important to note - let me repeat this once again - that in both cases, if they did actually occur, are very grievous cases, but on condition that they did happen, this was individual unlawful action on the part of individuals, on the part of individual policemen, and this is recorded in all countries. I'm well aware of that. Now, the question is how far that behaviour was prevalent and what the reactions to that kind of behaviour and conduct is. But we cannot generalise this matter and conclude that the police as a whole in Kosovo was violent and brutal and that there was a police state, as you termed it, in Kosovo. And of course both cases are to be condemned, that is not to be challenged at all, if they did indeed happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I really have now, I think, concluded with Kosovo. Can I make, however, for your assistance the following observations -- no, perhaps I'd better ask the witness one question first and then I'll come back.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: So far as Racak is concerned, Mr. Stevanovic, the materials you produce show, as is evidenced in this Court, that the KLA were present in Racak and indeed they did fire weapons on the morning of the 15th.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is shown by the materials that I read out and the information I had with respect to the event in Racak. And there are a series of operative informations, that is to say Official Notes, which speak of the activity of terrorists in Racak.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the way in which they jeopardised communication lines between Stimlje and Prizren, and Stimlje-Urosevac as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... try and keep you short. But the materials you've produced, the papers you produce, none of them gives a narrative account from an eyewitness of what happened, and it's all, so far as the Serb side is concerned, a matter of inference at best. Isn't that the reality?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the tabs, you will find a report on Racak or it contains a report on Racak compiled by the corresponding working group, and from that event we can see the sequence of activities on that day, what actions were taken and what each of the units did and what the consequences of their actions were. All the other documents show quite a bit more detail on it. Of course, all the details contained in the documents are based on knowledge before the event, knowledge about the event, and especially knowledge after the event, which is when the investigations were launched, with all the problems that we highlighted when we discussed the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And finally, although you may say you can't answer this I must make the suggestion so my position is clear: The documents prepared by the various Serb authorities avoid dealing with detail in order to obscure the truth and thus never cover issues like the recovery of weapons or the location of dead bodies. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean Racak itself, if that's what you have in mind with that question, then it is clear why those details are not there. They're not there because the documentation of the entire event was conducted after the situation changed on the spot, on the location.
